Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS): The severe hypoplasia of the left ventricle, the reduced mitral valve orifice, and the presence of interatrial and interventricular defects are consistent with HLHS, a condition characterized by the underdevelopment of the left side of the heart. The clinical presentation of progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency, along with the echocardiographic findings, supports this diagnosis.
Single Ventricle Heart Disease: The presence of a severely hypoplastic left ventricle, significant septal defects, and the functional single ventricle physiology (as suggested by the bidirectional shunting and the great vessels arising from the right ventricle) could also be indicative of single ventricle heart disease, where one ventricle is either missing or non-functional, and the other ventricle pumps blood to both the body and the lungs.
